brief:
A poll shows 70 percent of Jewish Israelis fear risks to election integrity ahead of October elections, Al Jazeera English reported. The survey reflects mounting concerns as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government faces growing criticism over the electoral process and governance.

The findings reveal substantial public anxiety about the fairness and security of the upcoming vote. Large majorities of respondents questioned whether the election will proceed without interference or irregularities. The timing of the poll coincides with intensifying political pressure on Netanyahu's administration and public debate over the state of democratic institutions in Israel.
dek: Poll shows 70 percent of Jewish Israelis fear election integrity risks as Netanyahu government faces mounting criticism.
title: Israeli voters express widespread doubts about election integrity
